methods.label: Double and track the jump number
methods.explanation:
One kilometer is \(1000\) meters, so we need the first jump whose distance exceeds \(1000\) meters. Starting with the first jump, repeatedly double the distance. The distances in meters are
\[
\begin{aligned}
&1,\ 2,\ 4,\ 8,\ 16,\ 32,\\
&64,\ 128,\ 256,\ 512,\ 1024.
\end{aligned}
\]
These are the first through eleventh jumps, respectively. The tenth jump is \(512\) meters, and every earlier jump is shorter. The eleventh jump is \(1024>1000\) meters, so it is the first to exceed one kilometer. The answer is the \(11\)th jump, choice C.
